title: Probability: Combined Events and Tree Diagrams
seo_title: Combined Probability – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Use the addition and multiplication rules; find probabilities of independent and mutually exclusive events; use tree diagrams, tables and conditional probability. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on probability: addition and multiplication rules, with and without replacement, tree diagrams, two-way tables and conditional probability. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).
  • Mutually exclusive events: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).
  • Without replacement, the second probability has one less in the total.

Examples

Example

Two coins

1/2 × 1/2

Answer: P(two heads) = 1/4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when the events happen together“And” means multiply.
Not changing the total without replacementTake 1 from the top and bottom.
Counting both orders onceRed then blue and blue then red are different.

faq.a: One event does not change the chance of the other.

items.q: A box holds 10 items. P(a fiction book) = 25 and P(a comic) = 110. One item is picked at random. Find P(a fiction book or a comic).
items.e: The events are mutually exclusive (one item cannot be both), so add: 25 + 110 = 12.

items.q: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.6 and P(A and B) = 0.1. Find P(A or B).
items.e: Addition Rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0.5 + 0.6 − 0.1 = 1. Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.

items.q: P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.6 and P(A and B) = 0.2. Find P(A or B).

items.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive (they cannot both happen). P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.1. Find P(A or B).
items.e: Mutually exclusive events have no overlap, so P(A and B) = 0 and P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.1 = 0.5.

items.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive (they cannot both happen). P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.1. Find P(A or B).

items.q: A number cube is rolled. What is the probability of an even number or a number greater than 4?
items.e: Even: 2, 4, 6. Greater than 4: 5, 6. Together: 2, 4, 5, 6, which is 4 outcomes. 4/6 = 23.

items.q: P(A) = 0.2, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.1. Find P(A or B).
items.e: Addition Rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) = 0.2 + 0.4 − 0.1 = 0.5. Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.
